A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same neural barrier function dialogue-steering work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original jailbreak-defense evaluations, helpfulness and over-refusal measurements, ablations, and qualitative analyses in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds evaluations of newer LLMs, additional alignment baselines, and sensitivity experiments in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: The dialogue dynamics, safety predictor, four training losses, and query-filtering procedure remain unchanged. The new Q-filter discussion clarifies existing inference behavior rather than introducing an additional algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v3 adds PHTest-Harmless to evaluate false refusals on pseudo-harmful benign prompts. Existing training data, attack scenarios, helpfulness benchmarks, RedQueen, and consolidated SafeMT_ATTACK_600/MHJ evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: New Table 13 adds LoRA DPO and LoRA KTO to the over-refusal and ActorAttack comparison on Llama-3-8b-instruct and Phi-4. This is a focused extension; the original prompt, SFT, and guardrail comparisons retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Additional experiments introduce GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 configurations, an ActorAttack-only training exclusion, an over-refusal threshold sweep extending to 5e-2, and controlled loss-weight sweeps over 10, 100, and 1000. Existing experiments retain their stated training budgets, data splits, metrics, and default hyperparameters.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands sensitivity and generalization analyses through loss-weight training curves in Figure 8, the ActorAttack-only holdout in Table 11, and broader over-refusal and MMLU threshold analyses. The earlier MTBench threshold curves and other ablations remain; the κ study moves into Section 5.3 without new results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the evaluations. The three-candidate sampling procedure for adaptive attacks is retained and does not constitute new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original tables and figure results are retained, while Tables 10, 11, 13, 15 and Figure 8 add substantial outcomes. For example, new Table 10 reports GPT-5 ActorAttack ASR of 0.355 without steering and 0.040 with steering. Table 15 partly tabulates existing threshold plots and adds MMLU results, but its Llama-3-8b MMLU at η=0 is 63.76, conflicting with 64.52 in retained Table 3.

T1.justification: Definitions 3.1 and 4.1, Theorem 4.2, Corollary 4.2.1, and the Appendix A derivations are retained. The query-context and Q-filter explanations add conceptual clarification without changing the formal assumptions, equations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about invariant dialogue safety, NBF filtering, generalization, and safety–helpfulness trade-offs. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v3 explains practical filtering through the Q-filter interpretation, interprets loss-weight sensitivity, and recommends η=5e-4 for balancing safety and utility. A new Broader Impact Statement discusses sensitive-topic filtering and safety-boundary biases. Appendix C's existing limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 documents the added sweep values, fixed-weight controls, and practical threshold recommendation. Existing architecture, training, hardware, and code-access disclosures remain; moving the repository link from the abstract to the introduction does not change availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds connections to Hamilton–Jacobi Q-filters, newer safety-certificate work, preference optimization, and conformal calibration, alongside references supporting new evaluations. The central positioning around dialogue-level neural barrier functions remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Focused additions clarify the method and expand Appendix B.2, introduce Broader Impact and Acknowledgments sections, and move the κ discussion into Section 5.3. Author information and citation style also change.

P2.justification: Four additional tables and a new six-panel loss-weight figure substantially expand the visual presentation. The κ table moves from the appendix to the main text, the first two figures exchange numbering, and journal formatting resizes and reflows displays. All original figure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The added preference-alignment comparisons, newer-model evaluations, and sensitivity studies improve empirical support and practical tuning guidance, while the Q-filter explanation clarifies implementation. These are useful extensions to an already substantial evaluation. Unexplained discrepancies between new and retained tables, including Tables 15 and 3, limit confidence in the added tuning evidence and keep the overall gain modest.
